walkthrough: Replace the separate key-event stack from yesterday with this forever-loop stack; keeping both would move the player twice. Control has orange forever and if blocks; Sensing has the key reporter.

when green flag clicked
go to x: -150 y: 0

steps: Start your own project or adapt your checkpoint
lessons.hint: Use what you already understand.
lessons.challenge: Explain your script without reading it verbatim.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Use your own project or checkpoint. Test Player movement and one Treasure body_entered signal before adding more objects. Say aloud what each script does.
walkthrough: Use your own project or checkpoint. Test Player movement and one Treasure body_entered signal before adding more objects. Say aloud what each script does.

lessons.title: Build the level
lessons.concept: A level arranges reusable rules in space.
lessons.recall: Can the player reach every item?
lessons.hint: Avoid unreachable corners.
lessons.challenge: Use an array to organize objects.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Place five Treasure scene instances. Player bounds are clamped inside the 800×450 viewport; keep objects within those reachable limits. Test every pickup, including corners.
walkthrough: Place five Treasure scene instances. Player bounds are clamped inside the 800×450 viewport; keep objects within those reachable limits. Test every pickup, including corners.

lessons.title: Add a fair challenge
lessons.concept: Difficulty should come from understandable rules.
steps: Tune player speed and hit areas
lessons.hint: Ask a new player before adding more hazards.
lessons.challenge: Add one moving hazard if time allows.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Use one hazard and leave a route around it. Adjust the Hazard CollisionShape2D radius and Player speed separately; test loss and the safe route after each change.
walkthrough: Use one hazard and leave a route around it. Adjust the Hazard CollisionShape2D radius and Player speed separately; test loss and the safe route after each change.

lessons.title: Finish the round
lessons.concept: Win, lose and replay turn a prototype into a game.
lessons.hint: Many bugs appear only after restart.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. finish(WON, ...) happens at target; lose calls finish(LOST, ...). Both stop scoring and movement. Use Replay after each ending and confirm all treasures, score and timer reset.
walkthrough: finish(WON, ...) happens at target; lose calls finish(LOST, ...). Both stop scoring and movement. Use Replay after each ending and confirm all treasures, score and timer reset.

lessons.title: Controller-friendly UI
lessons.concept: A handheld game must be usable without a mouse.
steps: Test navigating and starting with the controller
lessons.recall: Where did you still need a mouse?
lessons.hint: Use ui_accept and focus neighbors for buttons.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Set Button/CheckButton Focus Mode to All. Set focus neighbors between Replay and Mute, and grab_focus on Replay at start. Godot built-in ui_accept accepts keyboard/controller input. Test focus navigation on a real controller separately.

lessons.title: Catch-up and scope cut
lessons.concept: Removing unfinished extras can save a release.
steps: Remove an optional feature that is still broken
lessons.hint: One polished level is enough.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Save a working source copy. Fix one essential and remove an unfinished optional feature. Retest movement, pickup, both endings and replay.

lessons.title: Playtest on real hardware
lessons.concept: Computer success does not guarantee handheld usability.
steps: Run on Retroid with a parent
Record controls, text readability and performance
lessons.hint: Observe a new player without coaching.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Run on computer and on your Retroid with a parent. Record controller bindings, text size, sound and performance. Automated desktop tests cannot complete this hardware activity.

lessons.title: Fix the biggest bugs
lessons.concept: Prioritize crashes and broken rules before decoration.
steps: Check another player can start alone
lessons.hint: Keep a known-good backup.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Fix the most serious reproduced issue first. Replay win/loss/restart and try starting without help. Keep a known-good source copy.

lessons.title: Release checklist
lessons.concept: Source files and exports serve different purposes.
steps: Save and back up the source project
Export a working APK for the Retroid test device
lessons.recall: Which file lets you edit the game later?
lessons.hint: The APK plays; the Godot project edits.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Save the entire Godot source. With an adult, follow the linked Android export documentation for current SDK/JDK requirements, install export templates and export a test APK. Test that APK on the Retroid. Back up signing keys privately.
walkthrough: Save the entire Godot source. With an adult, follow the linked Android export documentation for current SDK/JDK requirements, install export templates and export a test APK. Test that APK on the Retroid. Back up signing keys privately.

lessons.title: Developer showcase
lessons.concept: Ownership means understanding the game and its code.
steps: Explain a function, signal and state
Make one independent change and rebuild
lessons.recall: What can you build next without AI writing it?
lessons.hint: A reference guide is allowed; explain your own decisions.
lessons.success: Check the described feature, then replay the project. Show your game, explain a function, signal and state, then change one rule and rebuild. Your own explanation and a physical export remain human/device checks.
